traces.reply: Hi Wrenfield Payroll, thanks for the details and the log lines. The signature is an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw request body, not of parsed JSON. In your code, express.json() parses the body and JSON.stringify(req.body) re-serializes it, which changes spacing and key order, so the HMAC will not match. Configure the webhook route to give you the raw bytes (for example express.raw({type: 'application/json'})), compute the HMAC over those, and compare with the Meridian-Signature header using a constant-time comparison. Details and other common causes are in [KB-013]. You can confirm the fix with Send test event in Settings > Webhooks. If you still see mismatches afterward, a support engineer will follow up.

traces.reply: Hi Kettleby Foods, sorry for the frustration. Here is how to rotate the key. Go to Settings > API keys and click Rotate next to the key. Meridian creates a new key with the same scopes. The old key keeps working for 24 hours, so it will not stop instantly and you can deploy the new key without downtime. After 24 hours the old key returns 401 Unauthorized. Because a contractor had access, you may prefer to revoke the old key instead, which stops it right away, so deploy the new key first. Full steps are in [KB-006]. Store the new key in a secrets manager or environment variable. If you need more help, a support engineer will follow up.
